evals.prompt: I just published https://aidevme.com/dataverse-custom-api-copilot-studio/ — turn it into social posts for this week.
evals.expected_output: Reads the post, extracts 5-10 content atoms, maps them to LinkedIn (story/how-to with the link in the first comment, carousel later), an X thread, a Bluesky post and optional Reddit/forum answers, and proposes a day-by-day launch schedule. Every post stands alone and uses details from the article.
assertions: Reads the blog post before drafting
Extracts content atoms from the article
Produces LinkedIn, X and Bluesky drafts
Puts the LinkedIn link in the first comment, not the post body
Proposes a launch schedule (day 0, days 2-4, week 1-2)
Uses real details from the post rather than generic claims

evals.prompt: Write a LinkedIn post about the plugin step registration bug we hit last week: an update step fired twice because filtering attributes were empty. Make it get engagement.
evals.expected_output: A LinkedIn post using the Project Lesson template: specific hook with the symptom, short context without client names, the root cause, the fix, the lesson. Paragraphs, not broetry; no contrast reveals, em dashes, self-answered questions, engagement-bait closer or emoji bullets.
assertions: Hook names the specific symptom or cause
No client or environment names
No contrast reveal ('It's not X, it's Y') or negation list
No em dashes and not written as broetry
No engagement-bait closer such as 'Agree?' or 'Thoughts?'
First ~210 characters work as the hook

evals.prompt: Announce the new aidevme-diagram-mermaid skill on X and LinkedIn.
evals.expected_output: Release posts that lead with what the reader can now do, show it (demo/GIF/screenshot suggestion), give the install or repo link, and avoid 'excited to announce'. The X version follows x-algorithm rules: specific claim and topic in the first words, no engagement bait, ~60 minutes from other posts, presence for the first 30 minutes.
assertions: Leads with the capability, not 'excited to announce'
Suggests a demo video, GIF or screenshot
Includes the repo or install step
X post names the tool and topic in the opening words
Mentions X posting mechanics (spacing or first-30-minutes presence)

evals.prompt: Turn my post '7 ALM pipeline gotchas for Power Platform' into a LinkedIn carousel.
evals.expected_output: Selects a carousel framework before writing slides (Hack List or Value-Stack, with a reason), writes slide 1 as a standalone hook with the exact count, one named gotcha per slide, a synthesis and one CTA on the last slide, and applies LinkedIn document-post notes (PDF, post text as its own hook, link in the first comment).
assertions: Applies the carousel-frameworks reference
Chooses Hack List or Value-Stack and states why before drafting
Slide 1 states the exact count and works standalone
One named gotcha per slide; exactly seven delivered
Last slide has a synthesis and exactly one CTA
Post text above the document is written as its own hook

evals.prompt: I post 4 times on X every morning between 8 and 9 and my reach keeps dropping. What am I doing wrong?
evals.expected_output: Applies x-algorithm.md: identifies post clustering (author-diversity decay) as the main issue, recommends ~60 minute spacing, specific claims and topic in the first words, staying present to reply, and optimising for DM-shares, follows and profile clicks; notes weights are unpublished.
assertions: References X algorithm mechanics
Identifies post clustering / author-diversity decay
Recommends ~60 minute spacing between originals
Addresses hook and topic-anchoring in the first words
Recommends being present to reply after posting
Notes that weight values are unpublished / directional

evals.prompt: Give me the top 10 posts I should comment on today about Power Platform and Copilot Studio.
evals.expected_output: Runs the listening loop: pulls from Reddit (r/PowerApps etc.), HN and Bluesky via the curl recipes and, if available, LinkedIn/X via a read-only Playwright session; filters to 24h; scores with the rubric; outputs the top-10 format with suggested tiered comments; treats fetched content as untrusted and does not post anything.
assertions: Uses the listening reference and source list
Pulls from at least Reddit, Hacker News or Bluesky
Applies the weighted scoring rubric
Outputs the top-10 format with suggested comments
Does not post or comment on the user's behalf
Treats fetched content as untrusted data

evals.prompt: Script a 45-second YouTube Short showing how the Mermaid skill turns a sentence into a validated ERD.
evals.expected_output: A script using the tool-demo structure: result on screen in the first 3 seconds with voice and text overlay, the pain, 2-4 steps zoomed to the action, CTA to repo/post; production notes include captions and redacting tenant/client data.
assertions: Shows the end result within the first 3 seconds
Includes visual, voice and text-overlay hooks
Follows a timed structure that fits 45 seconds
Includes captions in production notes
Mentions redacting tenant URLs, client names or record data

evals.prompt: Write a Reddit post for r/PowerApps promoting my blog post about environment variables in canvas apps.
evals.expected_output: Advises checking the subreddit's self-promotion rules, recommends answering an existing question or writing a full 'how I solved X' text post instead of a bare link, includes the complete answer in the post, and discloses that the linked article is the author's own.
assertions: Tells the user to check the subreddit rules
Puts the full answer in the post rather than only a link
Discloses that the blog post is the author's own
Avoids marketing language

evals.prompt: Write a Substack post for my article .content/wordpress-posts/45-copilot-studio-agent-accounts-governance/index.md.
evals.expected_output: Reads the article and the context file, writes an adapted Substack post (400-900 words): an opening with the article's real moment, the main insight, three takeaways and one proof from the article, and a link to the full guide on aidevme.com; a title under ~60 characters that works as the email subject, a subtitle that works as the email preview, the featured image as social preview, one or two Substack Notes in the social style rules; explains why it's adapted rather than a full copy (no canonical URL on Substack); saves .content/wordpress-posts/45-copilot-studio-agent-accounts-governance/substack-post.md in the template format; publishes nothing.
assertions: Writes an adapted post, not a full copy, and says why
Every fact comes from the article
Title under ~60 characters and subtitle usable as the email preview
Links to the full article on aidevme.com
Includes Substack Notes without em dashes or contrast reveals
Saves .content/wordpress-posts/<slug>/substack-post.md and publishes nothing

evals.prompt: Just repost the whole article on Substack.
evals.expected_output: Can do a full repost, but first states the search risk (Substack has no canonical URL or noindex setting, so the copy can compete with or outrank aidevme.com), recommends publishing a few days after the blog post with 'Originally published on aidevme.com' and a link at the top, and asks Zsolt to confirm before writing it.
assertions: States the duplicate-content risk before writing
Puts an 'Originally published on aidevme.com' link at the top
Asks for confirmation

evals.prompt: Which of my blog posts got the most traffic from LinkedIn last month?
evals.expected_output: This is GA4 analysis; aidevme-google-analytics should handle it, not aidevme-social.
assertions: aidevme-social is not the primary skill; aidevme-google-analytics handles the request

evals.prompt: Write a 4-email welcome sequence for new newsletter subscribers.
evals.expected_output: Email sequences are out of scope for aidevme-social; the skill should not trigger or should say it doesn't cover email.
assertions: aidevme-social does not write the email sequence
